requirement_text: AI risk management policies and procedures must be established, documented, and maintained. The organization shall define roles and responsibilities for AI system governance.
Organizational AI risk tolerance must be defined and documented. Risk thresholds should guide decisions about AI system design, deployment, and operation.
Clear lines of accountability and responsibility for AI system outcomes must be established. A designated AI risk management owner must be assigned.
Organizational workforce must be trained on AI risk management. Training programs should cover AI literacy, ethical considerations, and incident response procedures.
Policies for engaging with external stakeholders (vendors, customers, regulators) regarding AI risk must be established and maintained.
The context in which the AI system operates must be documented, including the intended use, deployment environment, and potential interactions with other systems.
Data used for AI system training, validation, and testing must be documented. Data provenance, quality, and potential biases must be assessed.
Potential risks and harms of the AI system must be identified and documented. This includes risks to individuals, organizations, and society.
Risks from third-party entities (data providers, model vendors, cloud services) must be identified and assessed. Supply chain risks for AI systems must be documented.
AI systems must be tested and evaluated for performance, safety, and reliability. Testing must include edge cases and adversarial scenarios.
Appropriate metrics for evaluating AI system trustworthiness must be defined and tracked. Metrics should cover accuracy, robustness, fairness, and privacy.
Continuous monitoring of AI system performance and impact must be implemented. Monitoring should detect drift, degradation, and emerging risks.
Feedback mechanisms for AI system users and affected parties must be established. Feedback should be used to improve the system and its governance.
Risk mitigation strategies must be developed and implemented for identified AI risks. Mitigation should follow a risk-based prioritization.
AI system incident response procedures must be established. Incidents must be documented, investigated, and reported to relevant stakeholders.
Change management procedures for AI system updates, retraining, and model modifications must be established. Changes must be assessed for new risks.
All AI risk management activities must be documented. Documentation should be maintained and accessible to relevant stakeholders.
Transparency about AI system capabilities, limitations, and risks must be maintained. Relevant information must be communicated to stakeholders.
Data security controls must be applied to AI system training, validation, and production data. This includes encryption, access controls, data integrity verification, and secure data pipelines.
AI model security must address model theft, model poisoning, adversarial inputs, and prompt injection. Model artifacts must be protected with access controls and integrity verification.
AI systems must undergo adversarial testing including red-teaming, robustness testing against perturbations, and evaluation of model behavior under malicious inputs.
Third-party AI models, datasets, and APIs must be assessed for security vulnerabilities, licensing restrictions, data provenance, and supply chain integrity before integration.
